NRC Primary
Our school supports children from Islington primary schools with Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs who have been permanently excluded, allocated a place through SEN consultation or via the Securing Education Board on a short-term placement. A high number of our pupils also have an additional diagnosis of autism and/or ADHD. We work with pupils whose special educational needs mean that accessing mainstream provision is too difficult for them and they require a higher level of support. We have small classrooms of up to six pupils, with a high staff-to-pupil ratio, ensuring that children are given the correct support when needed across the school day.
Using a trauma-informed approach, our staff work closely with pupils and families to develop positive relationships in order to remove barriers to learning and personal development. We believe that all behaviour is communication, and we base our approach on three core elements: celebration, restoration and de-escalation.
At NRC Primary, we offer a bespoke curriculum that supports children by identifying gaps in their learning and understanding. Our pupils also have opportunities to take part in activities such as swimming, music therapy and interventions led in partnership with the Educational Psychology service and Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services.
Using a person-centred approach, we work with pupils and their families towards a transition to a suitable future school placement. In the past, we have successfully reintegrated many students into mainstream provisions as well as specialist schools.
In the future, we hope to further develop our trauma-informed approach, supporting children and their families to overcome the barriers to education and helping them make progress with their personal development. We are passionate about building strong and positive relationships with the families who join our school and pride ourselves on supporting them to make progress during their time with us.
Carl Keegan and Karen GalvinCo-Heads of Centre

... our Executive Headteacher
I am very proud to be the Executive Head of New River College, which I joined in 2010. At NRC, we work hard to support all our pupils to learn and achieve in a safe and nurturing school environment. We are committed to helping them manage their emotions and behaviour and to acquire the skills they need for their next steps – whether that be returning to mainstream schooling, or moving on to further education or work.
Our pupils face many and varied challenges including feelings of rejection, failure and disillusionment with school; long periods without education and care; and lack of the specialist support they need to make progress. They also face the judgment and expectations of other people, who may not understand their challenges, and often underestimate their abilities and potential.
At New River College, we show our pupils that we care, in many different ways. We provide a safe, supportive learning space, personalised learning plans and support in every lesson and every intervention and support their personal development with a focus on their emotional health and wellbeing. We also look to their futures – using SEN strategies to support our younger pupils and providing relevant courses and career paths to help our older pupils progress onto further education and work.
To achieve the best outcomes for our young people, our committed and enthusiastic staff work closely with local agencies including Children and Adolescent Mental Health Services, family support, Safer School, occupational therapists, careers advisers, educational psychologists, and the Virtual School and social care professionals where necessary. We also have an outreach team that delivers training to Islington schools to help with their behaviour and special educational needs issues and which supports young people making the transition back into mainstream school.
For us, success means seeing our young people eager to attend school and learn. It’s also about seeing them make progress where often they haven’t before and ready to return to take their next steps – with confidence. Those we work with who are reintegrated into mainstream educations tend to do well. All our students leave with qualifications, and over the last 10 years, we’ve had virtually no students become NEET – not in education, employment or training. Some of our pupils have gone on to become head boys in mainstream schools, others to train as teachers, apply for a place at Cambridge and run their own businesses.
Looking to the future, I want to see all our young people get a fair deal – this isn’t always the case – and we will continue to get the message out that our pupils can and do succeed – with the right support and care.

NRC Medical
New River College Medical is an alternative provision for children and young people with medical and/or mental health and wellbeing needs. There are three branches to the provision:
Operating a trauma-informed approach to the education and care of all of our pupils, every individual has access to a broad and personalised curriculum, high-quality pastoral support and therapeutic interventions to capitalise on the talents and strengths of our pupils and build their confidence, independence and resilience. Progress is considered in a number of ways and targets are monitored and reviewed regularly by tutors, who are there to support pupils at each stage of their journey with us.
We work closely with parents and external agencies and, as a result, pupils flourish while at NRC Medical, often establishing the foundations to becoming their best self and fulfilling their future potential.
As the provisions continue to grow, we continue to network and explore a wide range of opportunities that our pupils need in order to equip themselves with the skills necessary to continue being safe and successful in their next steps, at post-16.
Helen Hopkins and Adam Sunderland

NRC Secondary
New River College Secondary is a school for 11- to 16-year-olds with social, emotional and mental health challenges. Pupils are taught in small form groups of generally no more than six pupils, with a high ratio of support from specialist teachers, learning assistants and pastoral mentors. Our pupils access a broad and balanced personalised curriculum that includes a strong emphasis on literacy skills, personal development, academic subjects and vocational courses. Pupils are fully assessed on entry during an induction week, and our flexible timetables are differentiated to meet individual learners' needs.
New River College aims to provide the pupils referred to us via Islington’s Securing Education Board with the tools and resources they need to make a positive transition from us, reintegrating into mainstream schools, or moving on to a specialist education establishment that will meet their needs, or into post-16 education, employment or training.
Our staff are supported by a variety of external agencies, such as Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), Safer Schools and Targeted Youth Support, to ensure that our pupils are safe and able to make the best possible progress. We are a trauma-informed school and the engaging and nurturing environment we provide encourages all pupils to achieve individual success and develop positive attitudes to learning, behaviour and relationships.
Bill Dimmock Head of Centre

CAMHS (Children and Adolescent Mental Health Service)
We have established a specialist CAMHS team in all NRC settings to make the service more accessible to young people and their families. Having dedicated CAMHS clinicians who spend a significant amount of time in the schools has the following benefits:
Our small team is made up of clinical psychologists, a child and adolescent psychotherapist and a clinical nurse specialist.
Young people come to NRC for many different reasons but they may have struggled with the pace of the school work, keeping to the rules of behaviour, or dealing with the size of classes or year groups in mainstream school. Some may have found their previous school environment overwhelming or emotionally distressing. Others arriving at NRC can feel they have been ‘singled out’ or treated unfairly in the past and that they have not been understood in their previous schools. Coming to NRC can be an opportunity to move forward, get support with things that have been difficult and find different ways of doing things. CAMHS is often a part of this process.
There are lots of different reasons why pupils at NRC and their parents/carers see someone from the CAMHS in the PRU team. Some examples of the kind of things we try and help children, young people (and their families) with include:

Our specialist team can help young people and their families in a variety of ways. As the team are based in the PRU sites, you will have the opportunity to meet a member of the team very early on, as part of the induction process to NRC.

Educational Psychology Service (EPS)
Educational psychologists are involved in enhancing the learning and development of all children and young people. They work with teachers, parents, carers and other professionals to help bring about positive changes. Educational psychologists work with five- and 16-year-olds who are on roll at New River College.
Our Educational Psychology Service focuses on improving outcomes for all children and young people by promoting learning, attainment and healthy emotional development. We aim to contribute to improved outcomes for all children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) so that they achieve their potential and are prepared for adult life. This involves working with families, schools and other providers to increase their capacity to meet a wider range of needs, as well as providing advice on individual pupils and undertaking direct work with children, young people and families.
We provide high-quality, evidence-based advice and assessment to inform outcome-based planning and intervention. We also work closely with other agencies to provide early intervention and support for children, young people and families (using the Early Help approach), and we contribute to improved partnerships and integrated working across Education, Health and Care. In addition, we support families and schools so that they know about and can make appropriate use of locally available services (the Local Offer).
All educational psychologists have had extensive training in all aspects of child development and learning, and are registered with the Health and Care Professions Council.

Speech and Language Therapy Service
Speech and language therapists work with children and young people aged five to16 years on the roll at New River College. We provide specialist support for children and young people with a range of needs affecting speech, spoken language and social communication. This may include difficulties in:
We offer a range of support that may include working directly with pupils as well as providing training and advice to help parents, teachers and support staff develop ways of helping children and young people to communicate more effectively and access the curriculum.
The Speech and Language Therapy Service is part of a multidisciplinary therapy service. We work collaboratively with parents, other health professionals and the child’s education team and/or wider team to support children to develop their speech, language and communication.
NRC's speech and language therapist is Nicoline van der Woerd, who works across all New River College sites.

Post-16 Progress Team
The Post-16 Progress Team provides help with a range of issues affecting young people, including career choices, college courses, job searches and leisure activities. The team can also connect you with agencies that can help with other issues such as benefits, health and housing.
The team is made up of experienced careers advisers (known as progress advisers) with qualifications in Careers Advice and Guidance to a minimum of NVQ Level 4. The service works with all Year 11 NRC pupils to support their next steps beyond Year 11 whether it is education (for example, at a college), employment or training such as an apprenticeship. All pupils will meet regularly with a progress adviser.
In addition, the service works with young people who are not currently in education, employment or training (NEET) after they have finished school and who may need additional support to stay on track after leaving New River College.
All of the information, advice and guidance that team members provide is completely independent, impartial and, importantly, confidential – no information about what is discussed will be shared with anyone else unless you agree, or are in danger.

The management committee
New River College is supported by a group of governors who form the management committee.
Working in partnership with the college’s Senior Leadership Team, these governors have a strategic and hands-on role in leading the alternative provision. Governors are keen to see the added value that pupils receive by attending NRC, which enables them to develop the skills they need to return to mainstream schooling or move on to specialist settings, college or the world of work.
NRC’s governors have a wide range of backgrounds and skills to draw on to support them in this pivotal leadership role (see NRC Governor biographies). Some are local headteachers and staff members who provide excellent advice on education based on their experiences of running successful schools; others bring a wealth of knowledge from a variety of backgrounds including business, finance, public sector, third sector, charities, legal services and construction. Our governors help to provide the challenge and support essential to the schools’ effective functioning and their skills have enabled NRC to make progress in a variety of areas.
For information on the governors’ declarations, checks and confirmations, click here.
Management committees
NRC’s management body is divided into three committees – Finance and Resources, Curriculum and Pay – each with a specific focus. Please click here to learn about the make-up of these committees.
Committee meetings
Click here for attendance at NRC Full Governing Body meetings for 2024-25.
Click here for attendance at NRC Full Governing Body meetings for 2025-26.
To view the governing body and committee meeting dates for 2025-26, click here.
Link governors
Link governors are members of, and are appointed by, the management committee to oversee specific aspects of governors’ responsibilities within the school. There is no legal requirement to appoint link governors, but they can be a highly effective way of helping the management committee to understand, oversee, monitor and develop a particular area of responsibility within the school. A link governor should ultimately enrich the whole management committee’s understanding of their particular area and contribute to informed decision making. Link governors are also a useful way for the management committee to develop positive links with staff and to maintain a visible and professional profile within the school.
Click on the link for a full list of NRC's link governors and their areas of responsibility.

Working with parents/carers
At New River College, we work in partnership with parents/carers and families. We know that this is the best way to ensure that your child fulfils their potential during the time they are with us.
We offer many opportunities for parents/carers to come into school and are looking to extend these opportunities further. We have held many successful charity events, coffee mornings and workshops. We invite representatives from organisations such as the Children and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), Islington Families Intensive Team (IFIT), Islington Healthy schools, educational psychologists and other outreach services to facilitate some of these sessions.
As we value your input and opinion, we will ask you to complete a questionnaire giving us feedback on how we can support you further. We also run a parent/carer surgery where professionals are available to answer your questions or signpost you in the right direction.
You will be invited to termly meetings to discuss your child’s progress with their teachers/support staff and to set new targets for their learning and their personal development. If you would like to know more about how you can become involved, please email Jo-anne Lee, Lead for Safeguarding and Child Protection, or call 0207 504 0534.

Careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) is an essential part of the support provided to students at New River College (NRC).
External organisations can access our Provider Access Policy here.
As a school, we have achieved the Quality in Careers Standard.
For students
We will support you throughout your time here to learn the new skills to be able to move forward. Year after year, more and more of our school leavers successfully move on to further education, apprenticeships/traineeships or employment with training. We have a high expectation that our students (you) will do well.

Your commitment to us
The effort you put into your learning and future planning will support your success. This includes:
For parents
Our programme of Alternative Curriculum and Careers Education helps our young people prepare for adult life, and this starts as soon as they arrive at New River College. Each student has access to our careers advisers. Through meetings with our qualified career team, employers, visiting speakers, off-site visits, work experience and RSHE lessons, students are supported to explore possible avenues they may take in the future so they can have the best start in life. All students from Years 7 to 11 take part in an annual Career Week, which takes place in January each year.
We foster close relationships with a number of local employers and further education providers to offer an employability-related Alternative Curriculum across all year groups.

pageCache.text:
Our Key Stage 3 curriculum has been designed to give our students the opportunity to gain a solid grounding in core subjects such as English, Maths, Science and Humanities, as well as the chance to explore and express their artistic and sporting talents through Art and Physical Education, and learn useful life skills through Food Skills and Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) lessons.

pageCache.pageTitle: New River College - KS4 Medical curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Key Stage 4 curriculum has been designed to give our students the opportunity to gain the qualifications they need to move on to further education, employment or training. We offer a broad range of qualifications from GCSEs in core subjects such as English, Maths and Science, as well as Art, to BTECs in Food Technology and awards in Physical Education and vocational options such as ICT, Animal Care and Hair and Beauty. Students also receive lessons in Personal Development and Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) to provide them with the life skills they need to thrive when they leave NRC.
